name: com.whogothacked/mcp
title: Who Got Hacked
description: Data breach records, each linked to a regulator filing or Have I Been Pwned.

tools.name: search_breaches
tools.description: Searches whogothacked.com's record for organizations by name or domain. Returns each match with its slug, incident count, the date its latest incident was first on record, the tier of that incident and source links. Records are verified from regulator filings and Have I Been Pwned; a threat actor's claim is never a source. A miss means there is no record here, not that no breach happened. Counts from different sources are not additive.

tools.name: check_organization
tools.description: Answers 'is there anything on record for this organization: a breach notice, an 8-K disclosure or a catalog entry?' from a domain or a name. At least one is required; a domain is tried first. found is true only for an exact domain or an exact name (case, punctuation and legal forms such as Inc. are ignored), and then every incident and its sources are returned. A parent domain or a similar name is never treated as the answer: those organizations are listed under candidates. Records are verified from regulator filings and Have I Been Pwned; a threat actor's claim is never a source. A miss means there is no record here, not that no breach happened. Counts from different sources are not additive.

domain.description: A domain such as example.com. This or `name` is required.

name.description: An organization name. This or `domain` is required.

tools.name: get_organization
tools.description: Full record for one organization by slug (as this server's results give it): every incident with its tier, dates, figures, data exposed, summary and the source records behind it. A California source record can carry `noticeLetter`, a passage quoted from its notice letter, with a credit line. A slug can be retired, for example when its organization is merged into another, or replaced after a rollback; a retired slug returns the current organization, with redirectedFrom naming the slug asked for. A slug that named a person who is not the organization (for example, an officer named in the filer's name) is withdrawn, not retired: it is not found (the API answers 404, with no redirect), and its organization goes on under another slug. Records are verified from regulator filings and Have I Been Pwned; a threat actor's claim is never a source. A miss means there is no record here, not that no breach happened. Counts from different sources are not additive.

slug.description: Organization slug, as this server's results give it.

tools.name: get_incident
tools.description: One incident by id (as this server's results give it) with its tier, dates, figures, summary and the source records that establish it. A California source record can carry `noticeLetter`, a passage quoted from its notice letter, with a credit line. An id can be retired, for example when its incident is merged into another, re-minted under its own organization, or replaced after a rollback; a retired id returns the current incident, with redirectedFrom naming the id asked for. An incident id made from a slug that named a person who is not the organization (for example, an officer named in the filer's name) is withdrawn, not retired: it is not found (the API answers 404, with no redirect), and its incident goes on under another id. Records are verified from regulator filings and Have I Been Pwned; a threat actor's claim is never a source. A miss means there is no record here, not that no breach happened. Counts from different sources are not additive.

tools.name: recent_breaches
tools.description: Incidents newest first by the date they were first on record, optionally within a date range. That date is a filing's date, or the day Have I Been Pwned added an entry to its catalog, and each incident's firstDateKind says which; it is not when the breach happened. Records are verified from regulator filings and Have I Been Pwned; a threat actor's claim is never a source. A miss means there is no record here, not that no breach happened. Counts from different sources are not additive.

tools.name: about_data
tools.description: How whogothacked.com verifies records, which sources it reads, how many records it holds and when each source was last read: the data's coverage and freshness. Records are verified from regulator filings and Have I Been Pwned; a threat actor's claim is never a source. A miss means there is no record here, not that no breach happened. Counts from different sources are not additive.
